node: Retail shelf access, private-label displacement and category control
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe around retailer shelf access, private-label displacement and category control. The reference lane is Walmart as the obvious asset owner and demand/control point: it owns shelf space, private brands, supplier data/analytics, retail media and fulfillment infrastructure. The underfollowed lane prioritizes companies that sit inside retailer-controlled programs rather than consumer-facing brands: SPS Commerce as retail EDI/data plumbing, TreeHouse Foods as a scaled private-brand manufacturer, and Advantage Solutions as a retail execution/category/private-brand services provider. These are research candidates only, not recommendations. Layer 1B expands the universe around the chokepoint where large retailers control shelf access, private-label programs, replenishment workflows, and category data. The reference lane is Walmart, because it owns the shelf/private-brand control point. The underfollowed lane emphasizes non-obvious public companies that either manufacture retailer private-label products, provide category/private-brand services, or supply the retail integration plumbing required for replenishment and compliance. No trading recommendation is implied. Expanded the universe for the retail shelf-access/private-label node using a two-lane funnel. Walmart is kept only as a reference anchor because its private-brand actions define the demand signal and retailer bargaining power. The underfollowed lane highlights public companies one or two steps away from the obvious consumer-brand battle: private-label manufacturing, retail
